meta.name: English
meta.title: GAMiq – The display system for halls and clubs
meta.description: Networked LED displays for basketball and training. No server, no app, no licence fees.

hero.eyebrow: The display system for halls and clubs
hero.lead: Networked LED displays that show what counts in any sport: shot clock, game time, score, possession. Every display has its role, and a phone in the browser operates it. No server, no app, no licence fees.
hero.note: We work out together what fits your club: a kit, finished units or something in between.

steps.title: A game day in four steps
steps.sub: Set up, switch on, scan the QR code, play. No installation, no technician.

items.d: Put it on a table or hang it on a wall or ceiling. Power by USB or built-in power supply.
The displays join the Wi-Fi, find each other and agree among themselves.
The phone opens the control page straight from the display. No app.
Everything from the phone. Up to three phones at once, or a tablet.
The platform is general; each game type brings its rules, display and controls. The game type is chosen on the phone.

items.t: Up to five displays, each with a role
items.d: Shot clock, game time, score: the role is set on the page, not on the hardware.

items.t: No server, no app, no licence fees
items.d: Everything runs on the displays and the phone needs only a browser. The software is free; no licence fees apply.

items.t: Up to three phones at once
items.d: The table officials share the work, or one tablet operates everything.
The displays find each other and agree which one runs the game. New software arrives over Wi-Fi without a cable.
Each court is a system of its own; rename and move units centrally.

types.title: Three today, more planned
types.sub: New game types arrive by update over Wi-Fi on the displays you already own. No new hardware, no opening the enclosure.

items.d: Shot clock, game time with possession arrow, score. Periods, overtime, 24 s and 14 s.
Each display shows a colour and the countdown. When it runs out the colours move on to the next station.
A time counts up to a target and a bar fills. As time, as bar or as one large figure.

types.soon_d: More game types are intended, with no date yet.
types.soon_ask: A particular sport in your club?

build.title: Five displays, three phones
build.sub: This is a basketball court in the largest build: a shot clock at each basket, the game time in the middle, one display each for home and guest. All units and all phones sit on the same Wi-Fi and stay in sync over it. Two displays are the normal case; the roles are freely set.
build.foot: * A table crew can also operate all units at once from one tablet.

roles.title: What each display shows and how it is operated
roles.sub: Every role has a tab on the web page. Beside it, the display in typical states, as it looks in the hall.

rows.d: 24 seconds, 14 after an offensive rebound. In the last 5 s the ring turns white and the digits red; at 0 the circle flashes.
Time with period, a strip per period and the arrow for the next throw-in.
Either home and guest together on one display, or one display each for home and guest. Up to 199; a rising digit flips once.
Each display shows a colour and the countdown to the change; then the colours move one station on. Up to five stations.
A time counts up to a target and a bar fills. As time with bar, as bar or as large minutes.

operate.title: Every official has a phone
operate.sub: On the phone the page shows the part of the role: the shot clock with pause and 14 s, the game time with period, the score with +1, +2, +3. Up to three phones are connected at once.
ticks: Scan the QR code on the display, done
Roles and game type are changed on the phone
German and English, switchable any time

hardware.title: Rugged, stackable, repairable by yourself
hardware.sub: 64×64 LED matrix, ESP32, 3D-printed enclosure. The colour of the corners shows which unit is which.
ticks: On a table, on a wall or on a ceiling
Open design: print files and bill of materials
